issues.legal_issue: A factual finding is not open to appellate interference when it is neither perverse nor based on no evidence.
material_facts: The appellant’s claim depended on proving possession of the disputed land in the relevant agricultural year.
The consolidation authority found that the appellant had not proved possession, and the revisional authority confirmed that finding.
The authorities gave cogent reasons for rejecting the possession claim, and the Supreme Court found no perversity or absence of evidence.
The High Court dismissed the petition challenging the revisional order, and the Supreme Court considered an appeal from that dismissal.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the factual finding and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A finding of fact is not open to challenge unless it is perverse or based on no evidence. The Court applied this standard in an appeal from the dismissal of a petition under Article 226 of the Constitution. No earlier cases were relied upon.

predicates.appellate_court_reviews_factual_finding: An appellate court is asked to review a factual finding made by a lower adjudicatory authority.
predicates.finding_is_not_perverse: The factual finding is not perverse.
predicates.finding_has_evidentiary_support: Some evidence supports the factual finding.
predicates.appellate_court_does_not_interfere_with_: The appellate court leaves the factual finding undisturbed.

issues.definition: When an appellate court reviews a factual finding that is neither perverse nor unsupported by evidence, it leaves that finding undisturbed.
